topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causes and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Intrinsic mutations versus environmental causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine whether cancer is primarily driven by unavoidable internal mutations or external environmental exposures.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, using the mechanisms underlying Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Mutagenic mechanisms of chemical and radiation carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens damage DNA, highlighting the role of xenobiotic metabolism in generating reactive mutagens.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, microenvironment, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic tumour promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and host developmental stages combine to facilitate malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, and laboratory methods used to identify carcinogens and prove their carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising the core themes and discussing how individuals weigh the risks and benefits of carcinogen exposures.
